jobs.description:
Job Description

Job Title:
Program Manager I - Emergency Response

Reports to:
Head of Programming

Department:
Programming

Location:
Nakivale or Rhino Camp

This position is open to Ugandan nationals only

Deadline:
Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to apply by October 23, 2026 no later than 5pm.

Please note that CRS is recruiting in anticipation of an award – recruitment for all candidates is contingent upon successful award of the project.

Background

CRS is seeking Program Manager candidates for an anticipated integrated Shelter and WASH Response for Newly Arrived Refugees and Persons with Specific Needs (PSNs) in Nakivale and Rhino Camp Refugee Settlements. The project will improve the protection, health, and living conditions of newly arrived refugees PSNs in Nakivale and Rhino Camp through increased access to safe shelter, household sanitation, safe water and improved hygiene practices. The position is expected to be based in Nakivale, with regular travel to Rhino Camp for supervision and program oversight.

Job Summary

As the Program Manager, you will lead the management and technical oversight of all Shelter and WASH related programming in the proposed refugee settlements. You will ensure effective systems and processes are in place to support high-quality programming that advances Catholic Relief Services' (CRS) mission of serving poor and vulnerable populations.

The Program Manager will be responsible for the overall planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of project activities in line with the project scope of work, results framework, and M&E plan. The successful candidate will provide technical guidance and capacity strengthening support to local partners and stakeholders and oversee project implementation across assigned geographic areas, ensuring quality, accountability, and timely delivery of results. Your management skills and knowledge will ensure that the CRS Uganda delivers high-quality programming and continuously works towards improving the impact of its emergency response and recovery programming.

Roles And Key Responsibilities

Provide management, guidance, and technical oversight of all Shelter and WASH program activities throughout the project cycle to ensure project design, start-up, implementation and close-out are in line with CRS quality principles and standards, donor guidelines, and industry best practices.
Effectively manage talent for emergency response and recovery programs and supervise. Manage team dynamics and staff well-being . Provide coaching, strategically tailored individual development plans, and complete performance management for direct reports.
Oversee technical assistance and capacity strengthening activities in emergency and humanitarian response for CRS staff, local partner organizations, government counterparts, and other relevant stakeholders to enhance preparedness, response capacity, program quality, and impact.
Provide technical leadership and assistance to strengthen humanitarian systems, policies, standards, and practices in Uganda. Support government, civil society, faith-based, and community actors to develop and operationalize frameworks, standard operating procedures, tools, and guidance at national and subnational levels.
Collaborate with the CRS Uganda Programming leadership and colleagues from the global CRS Humanitarian Response Department to identify, document, and disseminate lessons learned, promising practices, and innovations from proposed Shelter and WASH program. Support knowledge management, adaptive management, and the integration of evidence and learning into program design and implementation.
Contribute to the growth of CRS's emergency and humanitarian response portfolio by proactively identifying funding opportunities and supporting proposal development. Serve as a technical lead and/or writer for emergency and humanitarian response proposals, ensuring quality design, budgeting, staffing plans, and alignment with CRS and donor requirements.
Oversee the identification, assessment and strengthening of partnerships relevant to Shelter, WASH and emergency and humanitarian response, and the appropriate application of partnership concepts, tools and approaches.
Ensure timely and appropriate project expenditures in line with financial plans and efficient use and stewardship of project material sources.
Represent CRS in relevant coordination forums, clusters, and technical working groups, engaging effectively with government counterparts, donors, UN agencies, local partners, and other stakeholders to strengthen collaboration and advance humanitarian and program objectives.

Undertake other duties and responsibilities as assigned by the supervisor, consistent with the scope and level of the position, to support evolving programmatic priorities and advance the broader CRS Uganda emergency and humanitarian response portfolio.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Critical thinking and creative problem-solving skills with ability to make sound judgment.
Staff management experience and abilities that are conducive to a learning environment.
Experience using MS Windows and MS Office packages (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), Web Conferencing Applications, information management systems.
Good experience in project grants management, including project design, preferably for grants from multiple public donors, including US government and UN.
Demonstrated ability to write high quality technical proposals and reports.
Strong relations management abilities. Ability to relate to people at all levels internally and externally. Strategic in how you approach each relationship.
Strong presentation and facilitation skills.
Proactive, resourceful, solutions-oriented and results-oriented.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's Degree in International Development, International Relations, Community Development, or in the field of disaster management, WASH or engineering.
Demonstrated ability to convene, coordinate, and facilitate complex multi-stakeholder consultations and partnerships involving government, development partners, technical agencies, academia, and community stakeholders.

Required Languages
- Fluent English is required. Working proficiency in local language is a plus.

Travel
- include percentage of required travel, if applicable. Could be stated as Must be willing and able to travel up to 30 %.

Supervisory Responsibilities:
Yes, including but not limited to Project Officers and Senior Project Officers and project MEAL staff.

Key Working Relationships

Internal: CRS Country Representative, Head of Programs, Head of Operations, Uganda-based technical experts for MEAL, Gender, Youth and Social Inclusion (GYSI) and Partner Capacity Strengthening (PCS), Regional and Headquarters technical staff.

External: Local partner staff, representatives from for-profit and other non-profit organizations and relevant national, district, sub-county, parish and other government stakeholders, community leaders.

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in International Development, International Relations, Community Development, or in the field of disaster management, climate adaptation or resilience required.
Minimum of 5 years' experience inrelevant field-based project management experience.
Strong knowledge of Shelter, WASH and humanitarian response sectors, Uganda's coordination mechanisms, and protection principles to support safe, dignified, and effective planning, coordination, and program implementation.
Experience in managing moderately complex projects.
Experience in an international NGO.
Experience working closely with local partner organizations.

Agency Competencies (for All CRS Staff)

Personal Accountability – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions.
Acts with Integrity - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest.
Builds and Maintains Trust - Shows consistency between words and actions.
Collaborates with Others – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams.
Open to Learn – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things.

Agency Leadership Competencies

Lead Change – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation.
Develops and Recognizes Others – Builds the capacity of staff to reach their full potential and enhance team and agency performance.
Strategic Mindset – Understands role in translating, communicating, and implementing agency strategy and team priorities.

Please Note

CRS is an Equal Opportunity Employer: We encourage all qualified candidates to apply for this position, including individuals from marginalized backgrounds and people with disabilities. Please ensure you follow the instructions outlined below when applying.

This position is open to Ugandan nationals only.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to apply by October 23, 2026 no later than 5pm.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

About Us

Catholic Relief Services is the official international humanitarian agency of the Catholic community in the United States. Catholic Relief Services works to save, protect, and transform lives in need in more than 100 countries, without regard to race, religion or nationality. Catholic Relief Services’ relief and development work is accomplished through programs of emergency response, HIV, health, agriculture, education, microfinance, and peacebuilding. We welcome as a part of our staff people of all faiths and secular traditions who share our values and our commitment to serving those in need. CRS’ processes and policies reflect our commitment to safeguarding children and vulnerable adults from abuse and exploitation.

CRS welcomes candidates from the countries and regions in which we work. In the event the successful candidate is an expatriate, the anticipated duration of the assignment is informed by a term limit, based on the type and level of the job and the needs of the agency.

CRS is committed to safeguarding program participants, community members, staff and volunteers from all forms of exploitation and abuse.The successful candidate is expected to sign and adhere to CRS´ Code of Conduct.

CRS talent acquisition procedures reflect our commitment to safeguarding the rights and dignity of all people - especially children and vulnerable adults - to live free from abuse and harm.

CRS is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Technical Project Manager – Low Voltage, CCTV and Access Control based in Ireland.

We are seeking a proactive Technical Project Manager to oversee the delivery of low-voltage infrastructure, CCTV, access control, and networking projects from initial planning through completion. In this fully remote role, you will manage technical deployments across multiple locations while ensuring quality, efficiency, and client satisfaction. You will combine project management expertise with strong technical knowledge to develop accurate Bills of Materials (BOMs), define implementation requirements, and coordinate field operations. Working closely with sales teams, technicians, vendors, and clients, you will contribute to both pre-sales technical scoping and post-sales implementation. This position offers exposure to diverse security and networking technologies within a dynamic, nationwide IT services environment. It is an opportunity to take ownership of complex technical projects while collaborating with distributed teams.

Accountabilities

As Technical Project Manager, you will be responsible for coordinating technical deployments, supporting the sales process, and ensuring projects are delivered according to client specifications and operational standards.

Manage low-voltage infrastructure, CCTV, access control, and networking projects from kickoff to completion, ensuring timely delivery, quality control, and client satisfaction.
Develop accurate Bills of Materials (BOMs) and define technical requirements based on client specifications, floor plans, and site assessments.
Support the sales team with pre-sales technical scoping, including preparing quotes and proposals and conducting technical discovery calls.
Provide post-sales implementation support to ensure solutions are deployed effectively and meet agreed requirements.
Coordinate field technicians, vendors, and clients across multiple locations to ensure smooth project execution.
Oversee the deployment of low-voltage cabling, fiber-optic infrastructure, security systems, and network equipment.
Monitor project progress, address technical or operational challenges, and maintain clear communication with all stakeholders.
Ensure consistent implementation standards and reliable delivery across distributed project sites.

Requirements

The ideal candidate combines practical knowledge of low-voltage and security infrastructure with strong project coordination skills and the ability to manage technical deployments remotely. Excellent communication is essential when working with clients, vendors, and internal teams across different time zones.

Strong technical understanding of low-voltage cabling, fiber-optic infrastructure, and physical media installation.
Hands-on knowledge and project oversight experience with CCTV installations and access control systems.
Strong experience with Ubiquiti networking and security ecosystems, including UniFi and UniFi Protect.
Experience with point-to-point (P2P) wireless bridges and outdoor wireless infrastructure, either through fieldwork or project management.
Ability to develop Bills of Materials (BOMs), interpret floor plans, assess technical requirements, and scope implementation solutions.
Experience managing multi-site or nationwide field service deployments is a strong advantage.
Excellent written and verbal English communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with clients, vendors, and distributed teams across time zones.
Strong organizational, problem-solving, and coordination skills.
Ability to work independently and manage multiple technical projects in a fully remote environment.

100% remote working arrangement, with the flexibility to work from anywhere in the world.
Salary based on experience.

jobs.title: Implementation Manager
jobs.description:
We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is the foundation we build on; it's core to how we work, and we're committed to helping every new hire integrate it into their day-to-day. As part of our interview process, you'll complete a brief AI-focused exercise or discussion so we can understand how you think about and use AI to drive impact in your role. Feel free to reference any tools, platforms, or workflows you use today.

Role Overview

Benchling is building a world-class Professional Services team to drive implementations for our rapidly expanding customer base. Implementation Managers work with our customers, from small Biotech startups to the largest BioPharmas in the world to develop a deep understanding of their R&D Processes, and roll out solutions that transform how their research teams work together.

To be successful in this role, you will leverage your scientific background, project management skills, and product expertise to drive successful implementations of the Benchling platform. You will work hand in hand with the research scientists at our customers, and teams throughout Benchling to implement our solutions, and ensure our customers are successful. Implementation Managers lead all aspects of customer rollouts from requirements analysis and solution design, to configurations, testing, training, and onboarding users onto the system.

Responsibilities

Manage initial rollouts for new Benchling customers as well as expansion projects with new teams or for new processes at existing customers.
Own implementation success from project kickoff to go-live, leveraging strong project management skills, scientific expertise, and deep product knowledge.
Build and execute detailed project plans, own project activities, work with other team members to execute on project deliverables to ensure on time, on budget, high quality deployments.
Understand customers' scientific workflows and determine how Benchling can best be leveraged to meet their key business needs.
Lead requirements and design workshops, perform data modeling & application configuration, develop test plans and guide UAT execution, train and onboard users.
Act as a trusted advisor for customers, guiding them through the implementation ensuring they leverage and apply Benchling Best Practices.
Understand and document customer pain points, advocate for them internally to influence product changes.
Develop and optimize enterprise training programs including written and video collateral.
Identify and work with sales on opportunities for account expansion post go-live.

Qualifications

Degree in Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Immunology, Bioinformatics, Biological Engineering or a related field. Advanced degrees preferred.
At least 2 years of experience in a lab or research setting. You must be able to empathize with scientists and quickly understand complicated scientific concepts.
Strong communication skills. You must be able to quickly and effectively connect with a range of stakeholders, including scientists, IT project leads, and executives.
Self-starter with the ability to be successful in a startup environment.
Curious, creative, and tenacious. You should be excited to collaborate with customers and other Benchling teammates as a thought partner.
Ability to travel up to 25% based on customer and project needs.

Bonus If You Have

Experience using Benchling, especially if you’ve been a Benchling administrator.
Software Implementation experience, preferably with a SaaS software company.

How We Work

We offer a flexible hybrid work arrangement that prioritizes in-office collaboration. Employees are expected to be on-site 3 days per week (Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday).

#BI-Hybrid

Benchling welcomes everyone.

jobs.title: Protective Intelligence Analyst- OSINT Monitoring and Triage
jobs.description:
We are seeking a highly capable Protective Intelligence Analyst to support the protection of senior Vanguard executives globally. This role requires an experienced OSINT practitioner who can independently manage threat identification and triage, prioritize competing executive protection needs, and produce decision-ready intelligence products under time pressure. The position owns the threat identification and initial assessment function for Vanguard’s protective intelligence program, including the daily monitoring and alert queue through which every inbound threat communication, platform alert, and referral receives its initial assessment. The Protective Intelligence Analyst will distinguish credible concerns from noise, open cases for identified security concerns, and manage case tracking and related metrics for the program. The role offers broad exposure across the protective intelligence lifecycle and meaningful ownership of threat intake, applying structured analytic judgment to determine which matters warrant escalation or further investigation.

Monitoring & Triage

Manage daily alert and intake queues: vendor alerting feeds, the program’s intake channels, executive-assistant and partner referrals, and regional intelligence routing.
Triage inbound items against the program’s established threat screening criteria; disposition items as unfounded with documented rationale or open cases for investigation.
Provide dedicated monitoring coverage during executive travel and event windows, assessing emerging developments in real time and escalating per defined criteria.
Maintain watchlist hygiene and help fine tune OSINT feeds to ensure reliable threat identification.

Case Management & Intelligence Production

Maintain key protective intelligence trackers/metrics: request log, alert log, case entries, product IDs, and dashboard integrity.
Conduct OSINT collection and analysis for protective intelligence assessments, documenting sources and findings and contributing analytic judgments to final products.
Draft the program’s weekly intelligence summary, synthesizing alert activity, case developments, and emerging threat trends into concise, decision-ready reporting.
Process intake acknowledgements and maintain records-handling standards for intake channels.

Team Model – Primary Focus, Universal Capability

Triage and monitoring is the primary focus of this role, not an exclusive lane. Every Protective Intelligence Analyst trains to produce the program’s core assessment products to standard, rotates through triage and monitoring coverage, and serves as designated backup for at least one other product line, so the team carries no single points of failure.
Cross-train teammates in triage and monitoring, maintain current proficiency in teammates’ specialties, and participate in the program’s dual-review and after-action practices.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in criminal justice, intelligence studies, security studies, psychology, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
Minimum of three years of related experience in a field such as intelligence analysis, GSOC/watch operations, journalism/research, or military/law-enforcement analysis.
Demonstrated ability to work a high-volume queue with consistency, accuracy, and documented decisions.
Strong OSINT skills, including the ability to locate, verify, and assess the credibility of information across open sources.
Comfort with reading concerning or threatening content professionally and escalating appropriately.
High ethical standards and discretion when handling sensitive executive and corporate information.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to brief senior leaders clearly and calmly under time pressure.
Proven ability to think critically and assess incomplete, ambiguous, or conflicting information.

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on experience with threat intelligence, alerting, or case management platforms.
Formal training or applied experience in threat assessment, targeted violence prevention, or intelligence analysis.
ATAP membership, with active interest or progress toward obtaining the Certified Threat Manager (CTM) designation.

Special Factors

Participation in an on-call rotation for after-hours escalation support as the program matures.
Early-morning queue coverage; occasional evening and weekend surge coverage during executive travel windows.
Occasional domestic travel (

Special Factors

jobs.description:
The Central Investigations team is dedicated to keeping users of the Meta technologies safe. We pride ourselves in helping prevent harm by applying deep subject matter expertise to identify and mitigate potential safety-related threats to keep Meta and its users more secure. Our team is seeking an experienced investigator who will have the opportunity to work on some of the most challenging, high-visibility risks the company faces and the opportunity to have a substantial impact.We are seeking an investigator with experience in understanding and mitigating issues around terrorism, violent extremism, and other related harm types. In addition to having a demonstrated investigative and analytical background, we are seeking an investigator who has experience with open source investigations and who is committed to protecting people. The successful candidate will be able to assess and analyze large amounts of data in order to identify sources of potential threats and abuses, operate independently in a fast-paced environment, and proactively collaborate with teams across the company.

Investigations Analyst - Threats Responsibilities:

Investigate issues around terrorism and violent extremism and how they impact Meta, our products and our communities, with a focus on understanding how bad actors may try to utilize our family of apps and services
Investigate complex cases and conduct deep analysis of potential threats that may manifest on Meta technologies
Prioritize and manage concurrent analyzes based on threat severity, impact, and stakeholder needs
Identify sources of abusive behavior, quickly and accurately assessing the credibility of potential threats in order to mitigate risk of harm
Work cross-functionally with other analytic and investigative teams across the company, including collaborating with Policy, Engineering, and Integrity partners
Gather, analyse, and synthesize relevant data to identify potential abuse
Work with graphic and sensitive content on a regular basis
Make sound, timely decisions in time-sensitive threat scenarios with minimal supervision

Minimum Qualifications:

8+ years of professional experience in investigations or analysis in law enforcement, security, risk, or safety domains
Experience working with sensitive issues that include graphic violence, extremist content, a variety of religious and political views, and adult content
Experience analyzing large datasets to identify credible threat indicators and actionable intelligence
Subject matter knowledge on terror organizations and/or violent extremism actors, especially pertaining to various social media platforms, analytical tools, and online research tools
Experience handling and protecting highly confidential information
Experience communicating investigative findings and recommendations in writing to cross-functional stakeholders

Preferred Qualifications:

Experience working with a team spanning multiple locations/time zones
Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
Experience conducting open source investigations and/or investigations on behalf of a technology company
Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
Proficiency in languages other than English is preferred because the role involves investigating content and threats in specific non-English-speaking regions and communities served by Meta platforms
Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development and staying current with emerging AI technologies
Knowledge of data tools such as SQL, Python, or other data analytics programming coding languages and data visualization tools

Shape the future of America’s air-delivered deterrence. USSTRATCOM seeks an Air-Delivered Capabilities Analyst at Offutt AFB, Nebraska, to turn operational insight into capability decisions. You’ll assess bomber platforms, weapons, tankers, command-and-control systems, testing, and emerging technologies; translate warfighter needs into modernization and investment priorities; and brief senior leaders. Bomber employment experience is required. TS/SCI eligibility required.

The Air Force Civilian Service (AFCS) is looking for an Air Delivery Program Analyst (NH-0343-03) to work at USSTRATCOM/J87 at Offutt Air Force Base, Located in Bellevue, Nebraska.

In this position you will analyze, evaluate issues, develop recommendations, and determine necessary policies, regulations, directives, doctrine, and procedures in support of major command program(s). Supports development of Commander, USSTRATCOM (CDRUSSTRATCOM) Planning, Programming, Budgeting and Execution (PPBE) and Joint Capability Integration and Development Systems (JCIDS) submissions, major Defense Acquisition programs, and Congressional analyses. Additionally, supports air-delivered platforms, associated weapons, command and control (C2) architectures, and enabling capabilities/technologies development, modernization, recapitalization, force management, and analysis to include integrating, coordinating, prioritizing, and advocating for USSTRATCOM future concepts, mission capability needs, and weapon system development that directly affects the Department of Defense (DoD), United States Air Force (USAF), the air-delivered nuclear enterprise, and supporting inter-agency organizations.

This is a Direct Hiring Authority (DHA) position.

This position can close at any time. Apply Now!

Salary Range is $89,507 - $138,369 Annually based on experience.

Military retirement is non-taxable in Nebraska.

11 Federal Holidays each year
13 sick leave days earned per year (accumulative)

U.S. Citizenship

Knowledge of USSTRATCOM program goals, objectives, and operational plans and associated processes; the sequence and timing of key operational events and milestones; methods of evaluating the effectiveness of planning actions related to actual events; and the relationship of the various command entities involved in overall program planning and execution of military operations and evaluations.
Skill in designing and conducting comprehensive studies to evaluate an assigned program’s effectiveness and efficiency, preparing solutions to resolve substantive problems, and the ability to communicate findings to senior leaders.
Ability to plan, organize, and negotiate effectively with senior analysts and management for the identification, consideration, and resolution of issues that involve substantial resources and require extensive changes in established concepts and procedures.
Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing; negotiate complex issues; and maintain good working relationships.

Dedicated exclusively to children and their families, The Hospital for Sick Children (SickKids) is one of the largest and most respected paediatric healthcare centres in the world. As innovators in child health, we lead and partner to improve the health of children through the integration of healthcare, leading-edge research and education. Our reputation would not have been built - nor could it be maintained - without the skills, knowledge and experience of the extraordinary people who come to work here every day. SickKids is committed to ongoing learning and development, and features a caring and supportive work environment that combines exceptionally high standards of practice.

When you join SickKids, you become part of our community. We share a commitment and determination to fulfill our vision of Healthier Children. A Better World .

Don't miss out on the opportunity to work alongside the world's best in paediatric healthcare.

This position is part of the Occupational Hygiene and Safety team within the Occupational Health and Safety Services department. The position works closely with directors, managers, supervisors and project managers in Facilities Project Management Office (FPMO), Project Horizon & Early Works, Plant Operations, Information Services, Infection Prevention and Control, contractors and other departments, as required, to support the safe delivery of renovation and construction projects.

Responsible for management and supporting construction health and safety activities at SickKids, including providing specialized advice and technical support for contractor safety management across SickKids-owned and/or occupied properties.

Here's What You'll Do

Maintain implementation and ongoing improvement of the Contractor Safety Program.
Provide guidance and advice to hospital personnel, promote staff engagement, and support understanding of organizational and departmental project delivery processes.
Work with SickKids managers and supervisors to develop practical approaches that foster a safe work environment for hospital staff and contractors.
Build positive relationships with leaders and key stakeholders to support the Contractor Safety Program and related training and education in alignment with OHS regulatory requirements, standards, guidelines and best practices.
Monitor and analyze trends and new legislation, identify potential impacts, and recommend improvements to help mitigate risk.
Collaborate with leaders and project teams to develop evidence-informed solutions to OHS issues using a strong understanding of organizational practices and contractor safety management principles.
Regularly meet with FPMO, Project Horizon & Early Works, Information Services, Plant Operations, PGCRL and other stakeholders to identify upcoming and in-progress projects.
Interact regularly with Infection Prevention and Control (IPAC) regarding upcoming and ongoing projects.
Provide OHS input throughout project, renovation, maintenance and construction stages, including construction documentation, active construction and post-project review, to support compliance with applicable legislation, standards, guidelines and best practices.
Attend project-specific construction meetings.
Review contractor project-specific site safety plans and methods of procedure, as required, and identify concerns for follow-up.
Monitor contractor compliance with applicable health and safety requirements and standards through regular audits, and escalate significant issues as appropriate.
Lead and deliver orientation sessions on contractor health and safety for hospital personnel and contractors, as required.
Coordinate and participate in activity permit meetings, leading discussions within the position's area of expertise as required.
Conduct site inspections of construction projects, document contractor safety deficiencies, communicate findings to project managers, and collaborate on corrective actions.
Investigate reported staff health and safety concerns related to construction projects and coordinate follow-up with the appropriate stakeholders.
Review and maintain familiarity with SickKids hazardous substance inventory reports.
Support communications with external agencies (e.g., MLTSD) and liaise with subject-specific safety consultants (e.g., asbestos, lead), as required and in coordination with OHS leadership.
Perform other duties related to the position, as required.

Here's What You'll Need

University degree in Occupational Health and Safety or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education, technical training and directly related experience. Professional certification - CRSP, CIH or NCSO is preferred.
Minimum of five years of Occupational Health and Safety experience, preferably in a healthcare setting, including at least two years of construction or contractor safety experience.
Strong working knowledge of Ontario OHS legislation, COR certification, and other standards and best practices, with demonstrated experience in contractor and construction safety.
Training in the Fundamentals of Infection Control during Construction, Renovation and Maintenance of Healthcare Facilities and effective implementation of CSA Z317 is required, or must be completed at the next available course offering after the start date.
Strong analytical, time-management and organizational skills.
Demonstrated ability to coordinate work, influence stakeholders and provide technical guidance without direct authority.
Strong operational planning and prioritization skills, with the ability to contribute to program planning and improvement.
Strong interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills.
Sound judgment and problem-solving skills, including the ability to recognize when issues require escalation.
Demonstrated project coordination and program improvement skills.

jobs.description:
About Peregrine Solutions, Inc.

Peregrine Solutions hires top notch, top performing, hard-working professionals. We work as Owner Representatives to provide oversight of assigned construction projects and activities. Peregrine Solutions, Inc. offers competitive salaries, and provides our employees with paid medical, dental and vision insurance; three weeks' PTO, to be used at the discretion of the employee with approval from client; Federal holidays as recognized by the Office of Program Management; training and tuition reimbursement in areas directly related to field of employment; and provision of PPE including reimbursement for work boots and/or outer weather gear as required by project.

Project Manager / Quality Assurance – Fire Protection System Upgrade

About The Role

Peregrine Solutions is hiring an on-site Project Manager / Quality Assurance lead for a full fire alarm and life safety system replacement in an occupied, high-rise federal office building in Bethesda, MD. You will be the owner’s eyes on site. You will hold the installing contractor to the approved design, specifications and code, from mobilization through final acceptance and closeout.

Key Responsibilities

Serve as the day-to-day on-site lead and report to the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) and Project Manager.
Review contractor submittals, shop drawings, calculations and test procedures for completeness and compliance before approval.
Track RFIs, submittals and deficiencies to closure.
Inspect installation against the approved drawings and specifications. Produce daily reports and written site-visit compliance reports.
Act as Fire Prevention Program Manager during construction (NFPA 241): inspect all work areas daily, enforce hot-work, housekeeping and fire-watch rules, and report findings and corrective actions to the COR each day.
Manage fire protection impairments so coverage stays in place 24/7. Review impairment plans and schedule outages with the COR at least 14 days ahead.
Coordinate, witness and inspect mockups, preliminary testing and final acceptance testing with the owner’s Regional Fire Protection Engineer.
Oversee the switchover from the legacy system to the new one, and legacy demolition only after commissioning.
Coordinate and witness third-party firestop inspection hold points and ERCES radio coverage testing with the fire department.
Manage closeout: redline and final as-built drawings, O&M manuals, recorded training, spare parts inventory and warranty start.
Coordinate night work, escorts, outages and occupant notices with building management and tenant facilities staff.
Enforce document security (CUI/NDA) and site safety (OSHA 29 CFR 1926).

Required Qualifications

8+ years in fire alarm and life safety construction, with at least 5 years in a project management, QA or QC manager role.
NICET Level III or IV in Fire Alarm Systems, or a registered Professional Engineer (Fire Protection).
Hands-on experience with addressable emergency voice/alarm communication systems, including testing and acceptance in occupied buildings.
Working knowledge of NFPA 72, NFPA 101, NFPA 241, the International Building Code and GSA PBS-P100.
Experience managing fire protection impairments, fire watch and hot-work programs on active sites.
Experience on federal construction projects, including the submittal, RFI and daily reporting process.
OSHA 30-Hour Construction certification.
U.S. citizen, able to obtain and keep an HSPD-12 federal credential (PIV card) and pass a background investigation.
Available to work night shifts for the life of the project.
Strong written communication for daily reports, deficiency logs and test documentation.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Johnson Controls / Simplex fire alarm platforms, ideally with factory training.
USACE/NAVFAC Construction Quality Management (CQM) for Contractors certificate.
Familiarity with emergency responder radio systems (ERCES / in-building public safety communications), NFPA 1225 and radio coverage testing.
Knowledge of firestop inspection practice (ASTM E2174 / E2393) and working with third-party firestop inspectors.

Work Conditions And How To Apply

Employment type: Full-Time
Schedule: Primarily night shift in an occupied federal building. Some daytime coordination meetings.
Physical: Field work across all floors and below-grade levels, including ladders, ceiling spaces and mechanical rooms.
Compensation: $130,000 - $150,000
Start date: Contingent on contract award and badging
Relocation assistance and per diem are not available for this position. Local candidates are strongly preferred.

Benefits

Peregrine Solutions is a women-owned small business dedicated to fostering a collaborative and supportive work environment where leadership, initiative, and purpose-driven work are highly valued. We genuinely care about our employees, and the things that matter most to them. Our team communicates with clarity and intention, embraces hard work, and knows how to enjoy the journey together.

We offer a comprehensive and competitive benefits package that includes: Three weeks of paid time off, plus 11 Federal Holidays – giving you 26 days annually to focus on personal goals and recharge, 100% employer-paid health, dental, and vision insurance premiums, tuition and certification reimbursement to support your professional growth, employee referral bonuses.

At Peregrine Solutions, you won’t just find a job, you’ll find a community where your contributions are valued and your potential is supported.

If you are looking for a career shaping opportunity to support complex construction projects, we encourage you to apply to be part of the Peregrine Solutions team.

130,000 - 150,000 USD per year(Rockville MD)

jobs.title: Scientific Data Analyst II - VICD
jobs.description:
Job ID: req4683

Employee Type: exempt full-time

Division: Vaccine, Immunity and Cancer Directorate

Facility: Frederick: ATRF

Location: 8560 Progress Dr, Frederick, MD 21701 USA

The Frederick National Laboratory is operated by Leidos Biomedical Research, Inc. The lab addresses some of the most urgent and intractable problems in the biomedical sciences in cancer and AIDS, drug development and first-in-human clinical trials, applications of nanotechnology in medicine, and rapid response to emerging threats of infectious diseases.

Accountability, Compassion, Collaboration, Dedication, Integrity and Versatility; it's the FNL way.

Program Description

The Vaccine, Immunity and Cancer Directorate (VICD) has a primary mission to provide scientific leadership and laboratory infrastructure to study immune responses to Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines and other cancer preventive strategies in the context of preclinical and clinical studies. As of part of a recent large effort, the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) and the Frederick National Laboratory (FNL) and other stakeholders are developing and evaluating vaccines with durable protection against influenza. VICD is leading the development of immunoassays with the highest reproducibility, sensitivity, and specificity for evaluation of immune responses induced by vaccination in clinical trials.

The Vaccine, Immunity, and Cancer Directorate (VICD) at the Frederick National Laboratory has a primary mission to provide scientific leadership and laboratory infrastructure to study immune responses to Human Papillomavirus (HPV) vaccines, other cancer preventive strategies and other viruses in the context of clinical and pre-clinical studies.

Our core values of accountability, compassion, collaboration, dedication, integrity, and versatility serve as a guidepost for how we do our work every day in serving the public’s interest.

Key Roles/Responsibilities

The Scientific Data Analyst II will be responsible for working directly with VICD Director, Managers and laboratory staff to manage large datasets and conduct data analyses of immunological data, including serology assay data, flow cytometry and other data generated by the laboratory in support of large clinical and epidemiological studies. The incumbent will work closely with the Scientific Manager and laboratory staff to provide statistical analysis, data trending, power calculations and study design. This is an onsite work position. No telework option.

The Scientific Data Analyst Will

Build and manage databases to support large-scale immunological laboratory datasets.

Perform review of lab data and associated documentation for completeness, accuracy, and adherence to quality standards

Perform validations of templates used for data acquisition and analysis following pre-defined procedures.

Perform complex data analyses, data QC, and data interpretation in a timely manner within projected timelines.

Automate data collection and analysis processes for improved efficiency and reproducibility.

Prepare manual of procedures for data collection and data analyses.

Analyze large amounts of data to identify biomarker measurement trends and patterns employing new and existing tools to interpret, analyze, and visualize data.

Provide study design guidance to study investigators, such as power calculations and determine most appropriate statistical methods.

Identify appropriate statistical methodology needed to meet study objectives, include assay qualification and validation.

Perform statistical analyses of large, complex datasets from clinical trials and large epidemiological and longitudinal studies using appropriate statistical software packages.

Design and generate tables and graphs in publication-quality form, and present results to managers and directors in a regular basis.

Create databases and reports, develop algorithms and statistical models, and perform statistical analyses appropriate to data and reporting requirements.

Prepare and deliver reports for interim and final analyses, including data sections for quality control and validation proposals and reports.

Write and review statistical sections of study proposals, protocols, and manuscripts.

Review study proposals, including clinical trials and apply standards to create summary data reports.

Efficiently troubleshoot or report any unexpected technical and analytical problems.

Effectively communicate with all data generators and submitters to address requests, questions and concerns and clearly document actions taken.

Basic Qualifications

To be considered for this position, you must minimally meet the knowledge, skills, and abilities listed below:

Possession of a Master’s degree in Statistics, Computational Sciences, Data Sciences from an accredited college/university according to the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA) in a related field. Foreign degrees must be evaluated for U.S. equivalency.

In addition to the education requirement, a minimum of two (2) years of progressively responsible experience in data analyses.

Strong knowledge of statistics and scientific data analyses.

Experience working with databases containing large data sets.

Statistical programming languages such as R Script and SAS, applied to biomedical studies.

Experience in evaluation of assay performance by applying appropriate statistical trend analysis.

Strong analytical skills.

Experience with data management, Lab Information Management Systems and data transfer from different platforms.

Ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

Candidates with these desired skills will be given preferential consideration:

Ph.D. in Statistics, Computational Sciences, Data Sciences.

A minumum of five (5) years related data analyses experience.

Deep understanding and experience in processing high throughput biomedical data: data cleaning, normalization, analysis, interpretation and visualization.

Ability to understand and analyze data from complex experimental and epidemiological designs involving immunology, serology and biomarker assay data.

Proficiency with Python, R, MATLAB, or similar scientific programming languages.

Experience preparing scientific publications and presenting research findings in various technical and scientific forums.

Ability to understand and analyze data from complex experimental and epidemiological designs involving immunology, serology and biomarker assay data.

Experience in assay development, reference standard data analyses in GxP laboratory environment.

JOB HAZARDS

This position is subject to working with or has the potential for exposure to infectious material, requiring medical clearance and immunizations.

Commitment to Non-Discrimination

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, race, ethnicity, color, age, national origin, citizenship, religion, physical or mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, pregnancy, family structure, marital status, ancestry, domestic partner status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran or military status, or any other basis prohibited by law. Leidos will also consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories consistent with relevant laws.

Pay and Benefits

Pay and benefits are fundamental to any career decision. That's why we craft compensation packages that reflect the importance of the work we do for our customers. Employment benefits include competitive compensation, Health and Wellness programs, Income Protection, Paid Leave and Retirement. More details are available here

Position Overview

Syner-G is seeking an experienced Project Manager, Facility Readiness & Laboratory Relocation to support the planning, coordination, and execution of laboratory, office, warehouse, and utility infrastructure projects within regulated life sciences environments. This role serves as the primary liaison between project teams, engineering functions, Process Development, laboratory stakeholders, vendors, and facility operations to ensure successful facility build-out, equipment relocation, utility readiness, commissioning, qualification, and operational readiness activities.

Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to effectively communicate across all levels of an organization.

Manage the system's Risk Management Framework (RMF) process; prepare, coordinate, and submit security documentation for review and routing to the approving authority, and adapt to changing requirements from TBAI, Army CIO, or DoW.
Use the Enterprise Mission Assurance Support Service (eMASS) to obtain and maintain the system ATO; perform weekly continuous monitoring of ATO requirements, STIGs, and Control Correlation Identifiers (CCIs) and report weekly ATO status with a remediation plan.
Develop and maintain the RMF modernization and timeline plan with ATO milestones, and prepare and submit the ATO reauthorization package in eMASS before the current ATO expires.
Manage the vulnerability compliance report and lead annual contingency, security, and recovery tests, submitting documentation within 2 business days of test completion.
Prepare FISMA-compliant reports and update information assurance data in the Army Portfolio Management System (APMS), Army Asset & Vulnerability Tracking Resource (A&VTR), and eMASS.
Prepare and submit the Monthly Status Report (MSR) on RMF compliance, challenges, issues, and prior-month activity.
Serve as a member of the agency's Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT), acknowledging incidents within 15 minutes and initiating approved mitigation within one hour during duty hours; maintain the Emergency Operations Plan.
Review system change requests and recommend implementation or alternatives based on IA vulnerabilities within 2 business days.
Attend IA working groups, conferences, and recurring meetings virtually or in person, and provide minutes and recommendations within 2 business days.
Supervise the IA Analyst, review deliverables for quality, and provide backup coverage for IA Analyst tasks.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in computer science, cybersecurity, or a related field.
At least 6 years of technical and compliance experience maintaining a system's security posture and managing security within a Microsoft Azure Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) environment.
At least 2 years of experience leading teams.
Proven IA/cybersecurity experience managing the security posture of systems involving .NET, Windows, Azure, Oracle, and Red Hat.
Strong background in data architecture, the Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), and Red Hat and Windows security and administration.
Extensive experience implementing and auditing against DISA Security Technical Implementation Guide (STIG) checklists to oversee RMF processes and continuous monitoring.
Demonstrated ability to maintain a system's ATO and obtain a new ATO.
Experience using eMASS.
Strong technical writing, organizational, and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with technical staff, program leadership, and Government stakeholders.
Active favorably adjudicated Tier 3 (NACI) or higher federal background investigation prior to start.
Ability to obtain and maintain a DoD Common Access Card (CAC).

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with ACAS, SCAP Compliance Checker, and DISA STIG Viewer.
Experience supporting systems through RMF changes such as the transition from NIST SP 800-53 Revision 4 to Revision 5.
Experience supporting Army systems hosted in the cArmy Azure Cloud.
Experience with systems handling Privacy Act, PII, or HIPAA-protected data.
Experience with FISMA reporting in APMS and A&VTR.

Certifications

Active Tier 3 (NACI) or higher background investigation prior to start.

DoD 8570 IAT Level II certification (e.g., Security+ CE, CySA+, GSEC) required at time of hire and maintained throughout employment. CISSP satisfies both IAM Level II and IAT Level II.

jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Weekend Localization & Interpreting Project Manager based in France.

We are looking for an experienced and highly organized Project Manager to coordinate localization and interpreting projects in a fully remote, international environment. Acting as the key connection between clients and a global network of freelance translators and interpreters, you will oversee projects from initial planning through final delivery. You will manage budgets, timelines, resources, and quality standards while ensuring that every assignment meets client expectations. This role requires strong project management capabilities, excellent customer service, and a genuine interest in languages and cross-cultural communication. You will collaborate with clients and language professionals worldwide, balancing multiple priorities in a fast-paced operational environment. This is a full-time opportunity offering the chance to build a long-term career in the language services industry.

Accountabilities

As a Localization & Interpreting Project Manager, you will take ownership of the complete project lifecycle, ensuring efficient coordination, clear communication, financial control, and high-quality deliverables.

Evaluate project costs and prepare accurate budgets and quotations for clients.
Coordinate all project phases, estimate resource requirements, and establish realistic deadlines for successful delivery.
Use project management tools such as Plunet for time tracking and maintain full accountability for assignments from initiation to completion.
Monitor project progress, manage project status, and ensure that deadlines and quality expectations are consistently met.
Respond promptly and thoroughly to client inquiries through email, phone calls, and chat.
Maintain clear communication with colleagues through group chats, providing regular updates on ongoing tasks and project activities.
Negotiate deadlines and rates with freelance translators and interpreters using established freelancer databases.
Build and maintain strong professional relationships with language professionals across different countries and cultures.
Manage project finances, including budgeting and cost monitoring.
Perform quality checks throughout the project lifecycle, including proofreading and final reviews, to ensure accuracy and consistency.
Address freelancer questions and resolve operational issues efficiently.
Follow applicable internal policies, procedures, and quality standards.

Requirements

The ideal candidate has a background in project management, localization, interpreting, or customer service, along with excellent organizational skills and the ability to coordinate international stakeholders effectively.

Previous experience in project management, business administration, and customer service.
Knowledge of localization and interpreting processes, particularly within a project management environment.
Practical knowledge of CAT tools such as Smartcat and memoQ.
Experience using translation management systems such as Trados.
A university degree in Business Administration, Translation, or a related field is preferred.
Advanced written and spoken English proficiency (native-level or C1), along with fluency in at least one additional foreign language.
Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to prioritize tasks and manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Strong interpersonal and cross-cultural communication skills.
Professionalism, politeness, and a client-focused approach.
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, international environment and communicate proactively with clients, colleagues, and freelancers.
Full professional commitment during scheduled working hours is required. Job stacking and conflicting concurrent employment are not permitted.

Candidates must complete both the Emotional Intelligence and Wonderlic assessments after submitting their application.

Full-time employment opportunity.
Opportunity to work with international clients, translators, and interpreters.

Opportunity to develop long-term experience in project management and the global language services industry.
Dynamic, multicultural working environment.

jobs.description:
Application Close Date

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight! 

Blue Origin is pioneering the future of space-based communications with TeraWave, a revolutionary satellite communications network designed to deliver symmetrical data speeds of up to 6 Tbps anywhere on Earth. This multi-orbit constellation will consist of optically interconnected satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) and medium Earth orbit (MEO), providing enterprise-grade connectivity for critical operations worldwide.

Blue Origin is seeking an experienced Technical Program Manager to lead the end-to-end development and production of advanced communications systems. This role will coordinate complex, multidisciplinary programs spanning Systems Engineering, RF, digital hardware, ASIC, FPGA, embedded software, mechanical engineering, manufacturing, test, supply chain, and quality.

The ideal candidate combines strong technical depth with exceptional program leadership. This person will drive alignment across Communications Systems and Silicon Systems, manage dependencies and risks, and lead programs from system architecture and design through prototype development, integration, validation, manufacturing release, and production ramp.

Special Mentions

Relocation provided
Travel expected up to 20% of the time
Interviews will include a technical assessment

Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To

Lead end-to-end execution of complex communications systems development programs from concept through production.
Coordinate activities across Systems Engineering, RF, Digital Hardware, ASIC, FPGA, Embedded Software, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing, Test Engineering, Supply Chain, and Quality.
Develop and maintain integrated program schedules, milestones, dependencies, and critical paths.
Drive technical planning, program execution, and cross-functional communication throughout the product lifecycle.
Lead engineering program reviews, technical reviews, and executive status meetings.
Identify technical, schedule, manufacturing, supplier, and integration risks, and drive mitigation plans.
Coordinate prototype builds, hardware bring-up, system integration, validation, and verification activities.
Manage external vendors and engineering partners to ensure technical alignment, quality, and on-time delivery.
Drive action-item closure and accountability across multiple engineering organizations.
Record program and technical meetings, document decisions, and maintain a methodical system for tracking open items through closure.
Support design reviews, engineering change management, including ECOs, and manufacturing readiness reviews.
Partner with engineering leadership to balance technical tradeoffs, schedule, cost, quality, and product performance.
Develop executive dashboards, KPIs, and program metrics to communicate progress, risks, dependencies, and key decisions.
Drive programs through New Product Introduction (NPI), manufacturing release, and production ramp.
Identify cross-functional gaps and interface risks early, particularly across communications system and silicon development activities.
Ensure alignment of system requirements, interfaces, technical decisions, and deliverables across the product lifecycle.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
12+ years of experience leading complex technical programs involving multidisciplinary engineering teams.
Proven experience managing communications systems, networking, wireless, aerospace, satellite, or other complex hardware and software products.
Experience leading programs across the complete product lifecycle, including system architecture, design, prototype development, integration, validation and verification, manufacturing, production.
Experience coordinating cross-functional engineering organizations without direct authority.
Strong understanding of hardware and embedded systems development processes.
Experience managing technical schedules, dependencies, risks, issues, and executive communications.
Experience working with contract manufacturers, suppliers, and external development partners.
Demonstrated ability to understand complex technical issues and drive timely, data-informed decisions.
Excellent communication, leadership, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with satellite communications, wireless communications, networking, telecommunications, or aerospace systems.
Knowledge of RF systems, link budgets, digital hardware, PCB development, FPGA, ASIC, silicon, and embedded software development.
Experience with system integration, hardware validation, RF testing, EMC testing, environmental testing, and product qualification.
Experience supporting manufacturing readiness, NPI, production release, and production ramp.
Familiarity with Agile development methodologies and tools such as Jira, Confluence, and Microsoft Project.
PMP certification or equivalent program management certification.
Master’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related field.

Base Pay Range For

CA applicants is $269,175.00 - $376,843.95

Other Site Ranges May Differ

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description

Under the general direction of the Director, Health Major Capital, the Senior Project Manager (Sr. PM) manages multiple capital projects ranging from $50,000 to $500 million, ensuring delivery on schedule, within budget, and in alignment with quality, operational, and program requirements. The Sr. PM provides project management services throughout the project lifecycle, with primary responsibility for equipment planning, furniture, fixtures and equipment (FF&E), procurement, operational readiness, activation, occupancy, and closeout.

The Sr. PM leads and coordinates multidisciplinary teams including architects, engineers, contractors, equipment vendors, furniture suppliers, Information Technology, Supply Chain, Facilities Management, clinical users, regulatory agencies, and other UCSF stakeholders. Responsibilities include developing and managing equipment budgets, procurement and activation plans, project schedules, vendor and consultant agreements, relocations, and occupancy readiness.

Representing UCSF Health as an owner's representative, the Sr. PM supports new construction, expansions, renovations, and retrofit projects. The Sr. PM reviews design documents for equipment infrastructure, utilities, operational functionality, infection prevention, phasing, and fire/life safety requirements and coordinates equipment installation and activation to minimize project risk and ensure operational readiness.

The Sr. PM maintains accurate project schedules, budgets, forecasts, procurement records, activation milestones, and reporting using internal project management systems. The role supports Capital Budget development and ensures documentation is complete for occupancy, activation, project closeout, audit readiness, and informed decision-making.

Working with a high degree of autonomy, the Sr. PM exercises independent judgment in managing medium- to large-scale projects of moderate to difficult complexity and may coordinate the work of other Project Managers and Assistant Project Managers.

Key Skills

Develop and manage project, procurement, activation, occupancy, and close out schedules and budgets.
Maintain budget projections, cash flow forecasts, project records, and timely reporting.
Develop, administer, and monitor consultant, vendor, and procurement agreements.
Manage risks related to scope, schedule, budget, procurement, equipment delivery, installation, and operational readiness.
Review invoices, equipment purchases, and vendor payment requests for accuracy and completeness.
Lead FF&E, medical equipment, IT, signage, relocation, move management, activation, and operational transition activities.
Coordinate vendors, contractors, clinical departments, regulatory agencies, and UCSF support teams.
Ensure required documentation and readiness activities are completed before occupancy and activation.
Apply LEAN practices and identify opportunities to improve project delivery.
Build strong relationships across UCSF and foster a collaborative culture of accountability, trust, and integrity.

Position will work at all UCSF Health locations throughout the San Francisco Bay Area, including new off-campus lease sites. All Real Estate staff are required to be on-site, in-person, no less than four full days per week, although project activities may require additional on-site presence. The PM is required to be responsive to project needs and demands throughout planning, procurement, activation, occupancy, and project closeout.

Department Overview

The organization of UCSF Real Estate is focused on the development, planning, delivery, and management of physical space for UCSF. Key responsibilities include a unified approach to oversee the active UCSF growth planned on a multi-site campus and to manage the complex metropolitan environments affecting capital assets and projects and efforts to align municipal challenges with maximum effectiveness in support of the UCSF mission.

UCSF Real Estate is an integrated unit that enables the alignment of development, planning, design, construction, and management of facilities and a lease portfolio of 1 million square feet across UCSF.Services are provided through the following departments:Building Permit Services, Campus Design and Construction, Campus Planning, Construction Contract Administration, Health Design and Construction, Health Major Capital Projects, Real Estate Services, Benioff Children’s Hospital Oakland Capital Program Management and support through Business Intelligence, and Finance, Administration and Operations.

The Major Capital Project Department is responsible for delivering the design and construction of new buildings and other major capital projects as assigned. Typical project budgets are hundreds of millions of dollars. Our goals are delivered through Integrated Project Delivery (IPD) methodologies. Current project delivery methods include an IFOA contract. Our vision is to be recognized as an innovative and collaborative owner through new processes, innovation of new delivery models, contracts, and commercial terms that will attract the most qualified teams. Our projects are managed in the Integrated Center for Design and Construction (Big Room). Our work emphasizes the development of highly integrated and collaborative teamwork. We fully support and integrate Lean tools in our project work.

The combined UCSF Campus and Health organizations include approximately 198 UCSF and 38 contract personnel; operating/recharge budgets of more than $52.2M per year; current year capital project expenditures of $900 million; and oversight and responsibility for > $13.3 billion long-range capital development.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Architecture, Engineering, Construction Management, Planning or in a related field and three to five years of experience in managing all phases of capital projects; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Minimum 5years' experience in managing construction or renovation projects, preferably in a hospital, research laboratory or clinical environment.
Advanced knowledge of building and construction, design, construction contract administration and California Building Codes, including advanced understanding of industry practices, or deep expertise in a highly specialized and critical discipline.
Advanced project management skills to effectively manage highly complex projects, or highly specialized and critical project components.
Advanced analytical, organizational and problem recognition / avoidance / resolution skills.
Advanced written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, including highly effective negotiation skills and highly developed political acumen.
Advanced ability to manage contractors and maintain compliance to the agreed-upon scope of work and budget.
Demonstrated ability to simultaneously manage a large number of projects of varying size, type, and complexity.
Experience and ability to effectively lead and supervise staff and Project Teams.
Skilled in building, maintaining and nurturing strong professional relationships.
Financial skills to prepare, monitor and manage project budgets, evaluate cost estimates, and review payment requests.
Strong communication skills on a one-to-one basis or in a group setting with project team, leaders, stakeholders, contractors and consultants.
Strong Microsoft Office and project manager software skills. Working knowledge of CAD drawing programs or similar architectural design application programs.

Preferred Qualifications

Professional License in Architecture, Mechanical, Electrical or Civil Engineering
Experience with lean principles and process improvements.
Experience using Primavera Unifier and P6 Scheduling,MS Project Software or similar scheduling software.
Advanced knowledge of the organization, including its infrastructure, rules, regulations, policies and short and long range strategic building plans.
Strong project management skills to effectively manage multiphase projects or project components within an occupied academic medical center or academic research facility.
Knowledge of applicable building codes and / or regulatory requirements including, but not limited to, Title 24, OSHPD and the Americans with Disabilities Act.
Understanding and knowledge of industry practices. Ability to assess technical design documents, construction contracts, and related records.
Broad skills and technological knowledge in areas of architecture, construction, MEPF, Lean Construction and/or Project Delivery.
Knowledge of the organization, including its infrastructure and short- and long-range strategic building plans.
