new_jobs.description:
Application Close Date

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight! 

Blue Origin is pioneering the future of space-based communications with TeraWave, a revolutionary satellite communications network designed to deliver symmetrical data speeds of up to 6 Tbps anywhere on Earth. This multi-orbit constellation will consist of optically interconnected satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) and medium Earth orbit (MEO), providing enterprise-grade connectivity for critical operations worldwide.

Blue Origin is seeking an experienced Technical Program Manager to lead the end-to-end development and production of advanced communications systems. This role will coordinate complex, multidisciplinary programs spanning Systems Engineering, RF, digital hardware, ASIC, FPGA, embedded software, mechanical engineering, manufacturing, test, supply chain, and quality.

The ideal candidate combines strong technical depth with exceptional program leadership. This person will drive alignment across Communications Systems and Silicon Systems, manage dependencies and risks, and lead programs from system architecture and design through prototype development, integration, validation, manufacturing release, and production ramp.

Special Mentions

Relocation provided
Travel expected up to 20% of the time
Interviews will include a technical assessment

Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To

Lead end-to-end execution of complex communications systems development programs from concept through production.
Coordinate activities across Systems Engineering, RF, Digital Hardware, ASIC, FPGA, Embedded Software, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing, Test Engineering, Supply Chain, and Quality.
Develop and maintain integrated program schedules, milestones, dependencies, and critical paths.
Drive technical planning, program execution, and cross-functional communication throughout the product lifecycle.
Lead engineering program reviews, technical reviews, and executive status meetings.
Identify technical, schedule, manufacturing, supplier, and integration risks, and drive mitigation plans.
Coordinate prototype builds, hardware bring-up, system integration, validation, and verification activities.
Manage external vendors and engineering partners to ensure technical alignment, quality, and on-time delivery.
Drive action-item closure and accountability across multiple engineering organizations.
Record program and technical meetings, document decisions, and maintain a methodical system for tracking open items through closure.
Support design reviews, engineering change management, including ECOs, and manufacturing readiness reviews.
Partner with engineering leadership to balance technical tradeoffs, schedule, cost, quality, and product performance.
Develop executive dashboards, KPIs, and program metrics to communicate progress, risks, dependencies, and key decisions.
Drive programs through New Product Introduction (NPI), manufacturing release, and production ramp.
Identify cross-functional gaps and interface risks early, particularly across communications system and silicon development activities.
Ensure alignment of system requirements, interfaces, technical decisions, and deliverables across the product lifecycle.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
12+ years of experience leading complex technical programs involving multidisciplinary engineering teams.
Proven experience managing communications systems, networking, wireless, aerospace, satellite, or other complex hardware and software products.
Experience leading programs across the complete product lifecycle, including system architecture, design, prototype development, integration, validation and verification, manufacturing, production.
Experience coordinating cross-functional engineering organizations without direct authority.
Strong understanding of hardware and embedded systems development processes.
Experience managing technical schedules, dependencies, risks, issues, and executive communications.
Experience working with contract manufacturers, suppliers, and external development partners.
Demonstrated ability to understand complex technical issues and drive timely, data-informed decisions.
Excellent communication, leadership, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with satellite communications, wireless communications, networking, telecommunications, or aerospace systems.
Knowledge of RF systems, link budgets, digital hardware, PCB development, FPGA, ASIC, silicon, and embedded software development.
Experience with system integration, hardware validation, RF testing, EMC testing, environmental testing, and product qualification.
Experience supporting manufacturing readiness, NPI, production release, and production ramp.
Familiarity with Agile development methodologies and tools such as Jira, Confluence, and Microsoft Project.
PMP certification or equivalent program management certification.
Master’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Business Administration, or a related field.

CA applicants is $269,175.00 - $376,843.95

Other Site Ranges May Differ

new_jobs.title: Senior Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
Job Description

Under the general direction of the Director, Health Major Capital, the Senior Project Manager (Sr. PM) manages multiple capital projects ranging from $50,000 to $500 million, ensuring delivery on schedule, within budget, and in alignment with quality, operational, and program requirements. The Sr. PM provides project management services throughout the project lifecycle, with primary responsibility for equipment planning, furniture, fixtures and equipment (FF&E), procurement, operational readiness, activation, occupancy, and closeout.

The Sr. PM leads and coordinates multidisciplinary teams including architects, engineers, contractors, equipment vendors, furniture suppliers, Information Technology, Supply Chain, Facilities Management, clinical users, regulatory agencies, and other UCSF stakeholders. Responsibilities include developing and managing equipment budgets, procurement and activation plans, project schedules, vendor and consultant agreements, relocations, and occupancy readiness.

Representing UCSF Health as an owner's representative, the Sr. PM supports new construction, expansions, renovations, and retrofit projects. The Sr. PM reviews design documents for equipment infrastructure, utilities, operational functionality, infection prevention, phasing, and fire/life safety requirements and coordinates equipment installation and activation to minimize project risk and ensure operational readiness.

The Sr. PM maintains accurate project schedules, budgets, forecasts, procurement records, activation milestones, and reporting using internal project management systems. The role supports Capital Budget development and ensures documentation is complete for occupancy, activation, project closeout, audit readiness, and informed decision-making.

Working with a high degree of autonomy, the Sr. PM exercises independent judgment in managing medium- to large-scale projects of moderate to difficult complexity and may coordinate the work of other Project Managers and Assistant Project Managers.

Key Skills

Develop and manage project, procurement, activation, occupancy, and close out schedules and budgets.
Maintain budget projections, cash flow forecasts, project records, and timely reporting.
Develop, administer, and monitor consultant, vendor, and procurement agreements.
Manage risks related to scope, schedule, budget, procurement, equipment delivery, installation, and operational readiness.
Review invoices, equipment purchases, and vendor payment requests for accuracy and completeness.
Lead FF&E, medical equipment, IT, signage, relocation, move management, activation, and operational transition activities.
Coordinate vendors, contractors, clinical departments, regulatory agencies, and UCSF support teams.
Ensure required documentation and readiness activities are completed before occupancy and activation.
Apply LEAN practices and identify opportunities to improve project delivery.
Build strong relationships across UCSF and foster a collaborative culture of accountability, trust, and integrity.

Position will work at all UCSF Health locations throughout the San Francisco Bay Area, including new off-campus lease sites. All Real Estate staff are required to be on-site, in-person, no less than four full days per week, although project activities may require additional on-site presence. The PM is required to be responsive to project needs and demands throughout planning, procurement, activation, occupancy, and project closeout.

Department Overview

The organization of UCSF Real Estate is focused on the development, planning, delivery, and management of physical space for UCSF. Key responsibilities include a unified approach to oversee the active UCSF growth planned on a multi-site campus and to manage the complex metropolitan environments affecting capital assets and projects and efforts to align municipal challenges with maximum effectiveness in support of the UCSF mission.

UCSF Real Estate is an integrated unit that enables the alignment of development, planning, design, construction, and management of facilities and a lease portfolio of 1 million square feet across UCSF.Services are provided through the following departments:Building Permit Services, Campus Design and Construction, Campus Planning, Construction Contract Administration, Health Design and Construction, Health Major Capital Projects, Real Estate Services, Benioff Children’s Hospital Oakland Capital Program Management and support through Business Intelligence, and Finance, Administration and Operations.

The Major Capital Project Department is responsible for delivering the design and construction of new buildings and other major capital projects as assigned. Typical project budgets are hundreds of millions of dollars. Our goals are delivered through Integrated Project Delivery (IPD) methodologies. Current project delivery methods include an IFOA contract. Our vision is to be recognized as an innovative and collaborative owner through new processes, innovation of new delivery models, contracts, and commercial terms that will attract the most qualified teams. Our projects are managed in the Integrated Center for Design and Construction (Big Room). Our work emphasizes the development of highly integrated and collaborative teamwork. We fully support and integrate Lean tools in our project work.

The combined UCSF Campus and Health organizations include approximately 198 UCSF and 38 contract personnel; operating/recharge budgets of more than $52.2M per year; current year capital project expenditures of $900 million; and oversight and responsibility for > $13.3 billion long-range capital development.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Architecture, Engineering, Construction Management, Planning or in a related field and three to five years of experience in managing all phases of capital projects; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
Minimum 5years' experience in managing construction or renovation projects, preferably in a hospital, research laboratory or clinical environment.
Advanced knowledge of building and construction, design, construction contract administration and California Building Codes, including advanced understanding of industry practices, or deep expertise in a highly specialized and critical discipline.
Advanced project management skills to effectively manage highly complex projects, or highly specialized and critical project components.
Advanced analytical, organizational and problem recognition / avoidance / resolution skills.
Advanced written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, including highly effective negotiation skills and highly developed political acumen.
Advanced ability to manage contractors and maintain compliance to the agreed-upon scope of work and budget.
Demonstrated ability to simultaneously manage a large number of projects of varying size, type, and complexity.
Experience and ability to effectively lead and supervise staff and Project Teams.
Skilled in building, maintaining and nurturing strong professional relationships.
Financial skills to prepare, monitor and manage project budgets, evaluate cost estimates, and review payment requests.
Strong communication skills on a one-to-one basis or in a group setting with project team, leaders, stakeholders, contractors and consultants.
Strong Microsoft Office and project manager software skills. Working knowledge of CAD drawing programs or similar architectural design application programs.

Preferred Qualifications

Professional License in Architecture, Mechanical, Electrical or Civil Engineering
Experience with lean principles and process improvements.
Experience using Primavera Unifier and P6 Scheduling,MS Project Software or similar scheduling software.
Advanced knowledge of the organization, including its infrastructure, rules, regulations, policies and short and long range strategic building plans.
Strong project management skills to effectively manage multiphase projects or project components within an occupied academic medical center or academic research facility.
Knowledge of applicable building codes and / or regulatory requirements including, but not limited to, Title 24, OSHPD and the Americans with Disabilities Act.
Understanding and knowledge of industry practices. Ability to assess technical design documents, construction contracts, and related records.
Broad skills and technological knowledge in areas of architecture, construction, MEPF, Lean Construction and/or Project Delivery.
Knowledge of the organization, including its infrastructure and short- and long-range strategic building plans.
